fr.sorbonne_u.components.hem2025e3.equipments.batteries.sil

Class BatteriesStateSILModel

  • java.lang.Object
    • fr.sorbonne_u.devs_simulation.models.Model
      • fr.sorbonne_u.devs_simulation.models.AtomicModel
        • fr.sorbonne_u.components.hem2025e3.equipments.batteries.sil.BatteriesStateSILModel
  • All Implemented Interfaces:
    fr.sorbonne_u.components.cyphy.interfaces.ModelStateAccessI, BatteriesStateI, fr.sorbonne_u.devs_simulation.hioa.models.interfaces.VariableDefinitionsAndSharingI, fr.sorbonne_u.devs_simulation.hioa.models.interfaces.VariableInitialisationI, fr.sorbonne_u.devs_simulation.models.interfaces.AtomicModelI, fr.sorbonne_u.devs_simulation.models.interfaces.EventsExchangingI, fr.sorbonne_u.devs_simulation.models.interfaces.ModelI, java.io.Serializable

    @ModelExternalEvents(imported={SIL_StartCharging.class,SIL_StopCharging.class,CurrentBatteriesLevel.class},
                     exported={SIL_StartCharging.class,SIL_StopCharging.class})
public class BatteriesStateSILModel
extends fr.sorbonne_u.devs_simulation.models.AtomicModel
implements BatteriesStateI, fr.sorbonne_u.components.cyphy.interfaces.ModelStateAccessI
    The class BatteriesStateSILModel implements a simulation model managing the state for the batteries.

    Description

    In the batteries SIL simulation, as the batteries model simulating the power consumption and production must be co-located with the electric meter models, this model will be executed within the batteries component to bridge the gap between the batteries component code that may change the state and the power model that must keep track of these changes. This state model receives events like starting and stopping the charge of the batteries, update its own state tracking and resends the events to the batteries power consumption and production model.

    The batteries power consumption and production model also keeps track of the charge level of the batteries, which is also an information that the batteries component code needs to access. Because the component code cannot access an information kept in a simulation model held by another component, the charge level must be sent back to this state model in order to be accessible within the batteries component. To do so, a new event called CurrentBatteriesLevel is added that is exported by the power model and imported by the state model. Each time the power model considers that a significant change in the charge level must be forwarded to the state model, it sends a CurrentBatteriesLevel, which is received and processed by the state model.

    See BatteriesPowerSILModel.

    • Imported events: SIL_StartCharging, SIL_StopCharging, CurrentBatteriesLevel
    • Exported events: SIL_StartCharging, SIL_StopCharging

        public BatteriesStateSILModel(java.lang.String uri,
                              java.util.concurrent.TimeUnit simulatedTimeUnit,
                              fr.sorbonne_u.devs_simulation.simulators.interfaces.AtomicSimulatorI simulationEngine)
        create an atomic model with the given URI (if null, one will be generated) and to be run by the given simulator using the given time unit for its clock.

        Contract

         pre     uri == null || !uri.isEmpty()
 pre     simulatedTimeUnit != null
 pre     simulationEngine != null && !simulationEngine.isModelSet()
 pre     simulationEngine instanceof AtomicEngine
 post    !isDebugModeOn()
 post    getURI() != null && !getURI().isEmpty()
 post    uri == null || getURI().equals(uri)
 post    getSimulatedTimeUnit().equals(simulatedTimeUnit)
 post    getSimulationEngine().equals(simulationEngine)
        Parameters:
        uri - unique identifier of the model.
        simulatedTimeUnit - time unit used for the simulation clock.
        simulationEngine - simulation engine enacting the model.
